subject: science
chapter_title: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures

concepts.title: Mixtures and Their Kinds
concepts.definition: A mixture is a combination of two or more substances that keep their own identities; poha or sprout salad is a visible heterogeneous mixture while salt dissolved in water is a uniform homogeneous mixture, and the parts of any mixture can be separated by physical methods.
concepts.key_idea: In a mixture nothing new is made - the ingredients keep their properties and can be picked apart physically.
question_patterns: define a mixture with two examples from daily life
differentiate homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures with examples
why can the components of a mixture be separated by physical methods
is salt solution a mixture - justify
list methods of separating mixtures
what happens to the properties of substances in a mixture

solution_steps.explain: Two or more substances are simply brought together, no new substance forms.
Same composition throughout makes it homogeneous; visible parts make it heterogeneous.
Filtration, evaporation, winnowing or magnets undo the mixing physically.

concepts.title: Pure Substances
concepts.definition: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle throughout - it cannot be split by physical means; elements and compounds are the two families of pure substances, unlike mixtures which blend several substances.
concepts.key_idea: One kind of particle everywhere: that is the signature of a pure substance.
question_patterns: what is a pure substance - define it
how does a pure substance differ from a mixture
can a pure substance be separated by physical methods - justify
give two examples of pure substances
why is distilled water called pure
which pure substance is made of one kind of atom only

solution_steps.explain: Only one type of particle may be present throughout the sample.
Physical methods cannot break it into different substances.
The pure substance is either an element or a compound.

concepts.title: Elements and Compounds
concepts.definition: An element is a pure substance made of a single kind of atom - iron, copper, oxygen, hydrogen - while a compound forms when atoms of different elements chemically join in fixed ratios, as water joins hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed proportion, giving a substance with its own new properties.
concepts.key_idea: Elements are single-atom substances; compounds are chemical unions in fixed ratios with brand-new properties.
question_patterns: define element and compound with examples
how is a compound different from a mixture
why do water and its elements hydrogen and oxygen have different properties
name five common elements and their symbols
what is meant by a fixed ratio in a compound
classify iron, salt, oxygen and air into element, compound and mixture

solution_steps.explain: One kind of atom means an element; two or more chemically bound means a compound.
In a compound the elements sit in a fixed mass ratio, unlike a mixture.
A compound behaves nothing like its parent elements, so chemical union is proved.

concepts.title: Using Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
concepts.definition: Knowing what a material is made of tells us how to use and handle it: metals from elements build wires and tools, compounds like salt and sugar serve as food chemicals, and deliberately mixed alloys and solutions give materials with chosen properties.
concepts.key_idea: Classification guides application: pick, combine and separate substances by their class.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu108.txt lines 763-805 (how do we use elements, compounds, mixtures)
question_patterns: give one everyday use of an element, a compound and a mixture
why are alloys made by mixing metals
how does classification of matter help in daily life

name a compound used in cooking and its elements
how do jewellers use mixtures of metals

solution_steps.explain: Decide element, compound or mixture from its composition.
Conductivity, hardness, taste and solubility follow from the class.
Uses match properties: copper wires, salt in food, alloys for strength.

concepts.title: Minerals
concepts.definition: Minerals are naturally occurring substances in rocks and ores from which metals and other useful materials are obtained; iron, aluminium and gold reach us after extraction and purification of their minerals.
concepts.key_idea: Minerals are nature's storehouse of elements and compounds locked in rocks.
question_patterns: what are minerals - define with examples
how do we obtain metals from minerals
name the mineral from which iron is extracted
why are minerals called natural resources
distinguish an ore from a mineral
list minerals used in daily life and their sources

solution_steps.explain: Minerals occur naturally in the earth's crust inside rocks and ores.
Mining and purification separate the desired metal or compound.
Utensils, wires, jewellery and cement all trace back to minerals.
